Explain in your own words what 'Circular Flow of Income' refers to.
questions.a: The circular flow of income illustrates the continuous flow of goods, services and factor payments between firms and households in an economy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Circular Flow of Income'.
questions.a: Production generates income, income generates expenditure, and expenditure generates production in a circular manner.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Circular Flow of Income' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Introduction

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Nominal GDP and Real GDP' refers to.
questions.a: Nominal GDP is measured at current prices; real GDP is measured at constant base-year prices, removing the effect of price changes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Nominal GDP and Real GDP'.
questions.a: Real GDP reflects true changes in physical output by holding prices constant.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Nominal GDP and Real GDP', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Real GDP = Nominal GDP / GDP deflator x 100

questions.q: Using the method 'GDP Deflator', work with: constant_price_gdp = 500, current_price_gdp = 8000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of gdp_deflator.
questions.a: 1600 per cent

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'GDP Deflator' and work with: constant_price_gdp = 8000, current_price_gdp = 20000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of gdp_deflator.
questions.a: 250 per cent

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'GDP Deflator' refers to.
questions.a: The GDP deflator is the ratio of nominal GDP to real GDP multiplied by 100; it measures the overall price level of all goods and services in GDP.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'GDP Deflator'.
questions.a: The deflator reflects price changes between the current year and the base year.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'GDP Deflator', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: GDP Deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) x 100

questions.a: 5350 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Measurement of National Income: Value Added Method' refers to.
questions.a: The value added method estimates national income by summing the value added by each producing unit in the economy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Measurement of National Income: Value Added Method'.
questions.a: Value added avoids double counting by excluding the value of intermediate goods.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Measurement of National Income: Value Added Method', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Value Added = Value of Output - Intermediate Consumption; GDP = sum of value added

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Measurement of National Income: Expenditure Method' refers to.
questions.a: The expenditure method estimates GDP by summing final consumption expenditure, investment expenditure and net exports.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Measurement of National Income: Expenditure Method'.
questions.a: National income is obtained by aggregating final expenditures on goods and services.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Measurement of National Income: Expenditure Method', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: GDP = C + I + G + (X - M)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'GDP and Welfare' refers to.
questions.a: GDP is often used as an indicator of welfare, but higher GDP does not always mean higher welfare due to distribution, composition and non-monetary factors.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'GDP and Welfare'.
questions.a: GDP growth is necessary but not sufficient for welfare improvement.

questions.q: Under which section is 'GDP and Welfare' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: GDP and Welfare
